---
title: "Retrieval-Augmented Prediction for Tabular Foundation Models under Heavy Class Imbalance"
subtitle: "Test-time context construction for in-context-learning fraud detection"
author: "Theo"
date: today
abstract: |
  Financial fraud detection is an extreme imbalanced-learning problem: fraudulent
  records form a tiny fraction of all activity, yet the cost of missing them is high.
  Tabular foundation models (FTMs) such as the TabPFN family and TabICLv2 have recently
  matched or surpassed gradient-boosted decision trees on tabular classification through
  in-context learning, predicting by conditioning on a training context at inference time
  rather than by training a model per dataset. These models, however, have a fixed and
  modest context window, and under heavy class imbalance the standard practice of filling
  it by uniform random subsampling wastes almost the entire window on redundant legitimate
  records while admitting only a handful of fraud examples. This thesis proposes
  Retrieval-Augmented Prediction (RAP), a test-time context-construction strategy that, for
  each batch of records to be scored, retrieves a structurally similar context by
  k-nearest-neighbour search and rebalances it to a controlled fraud ratio by oversampling.
  RAP operates entirely at inference on a frozen model and requires no retraining. We
  evaluate five FTMs and two gradient-boosted baselines on six public fraud-detection
  datasets, using prevalence-corrected PR-AUC and recall at fixed false-positive rates, and
  decompose RAP's benefit into a relevance component (retrieval) and a ratio component
  (oversampling).
format:
